observations.finding: At identical display contrast treated 0.3uM fields (4) vs DMSO show similar confluence with irregular black gaps; no massive cell loss. 635 cells measured. DNA blue nuclei are modestly larger, more spread, still round/oval smooth. No fragmentation, pyknosis or multipolar mitoses accumulation. Rare very large nuclei visible, consistent with increased large-nucleus fraction.

DNA blue nuclei show increased size measured: nuc_area 1107 vs DMSO median 809 (z=+23.6), nuc_major_axis 41.4 vs 36.7 (z=+12.1), frac_large_nucleus 0.021 vs 0.008 (z=+4.3). Only composites available, but visual enlargement and rare giant nuclei support.

DNA blue nuclei show increased DNA content integrated intensity: nuc_dna_integrated 500.8 vs 327.2 (z=+5.6) and marginally higher solidity 0.975 vs 0.973 (z=+5.8). Treated nuclei appear if anything slightly brighter blue at same contrast; increase is largely due to larger area. Still smooth oval.
DNA blue nuclei show no obvious increase in mitotic figures beyond DMSO; no Eg5-like monopolar rosettes or microtubule bundling seen.

beta-tubulin green radial array intact, perinuclear enriched, extends to periphery. No depolymerization (loss of green) nor stabilization (thick bundles) vs DMSO. Intensity and morphology comparable in all fields.
F-actin red cortical/belt and stress fiber network intact; no puncta or collapse as in actin disruptors. If anything cells flatter/smoother.
cell shape: cell_area 5257 vs 3406 (z=+5.4), cell_major_axis 110.2 vs 87.6 (z=+5.4) - visibly larger footprint, elongated/spread cells and 1-2 giant cells per field. Consistent.

F-actin red texture: act_glcm_contrast -4.13 (0.001 vs 0.001 median rounded) reported as strong decrease. Visually no increase in contrast; actin appears similar to DMSO, slightly smoother in enlarged flat cells, consistent with no disruptor phenotype but subtle smoothing expected in larger cells.

reflection.text:
Unblinded compound is mitomycin C (CID 5746) - ChEMBL 'DNA inhibitor' on NUCLEIC-ACID, and literature returned in this run confirms mechanism as crosslinker/DNA-damager: PMID 41199376 mitomycin C-induced DSBs and PMID 17512921 mitomycin C-DNA interstrand crosslink, plus general cross-linker biology PMID 8562965. Verdict correct: we called DNA damage at p=0.58, truth DNA damage. Calibration was appropriate - we did not claim high confidence, and runner-up DNA replication at 0.22 was explicitly retained.

What got it right:
- Acquisition choice to sample across dynamic range was discriminative. e2 (0.3 uM) and e3 (3 uM) both showed extreme, concordant nuclear phenotype: nuc_area z=+23.6 and +26.7, nuc_major_axis +12.1/+15.3, nuc_dna_integrated +14.0 at 3 uM - consistent with G2 arrest/DNA content increase, not focal toxicity. e4 (0.003 uM) established inactive baseline (nuc_dna_mean +5.2 only modest) and e5 (10 uM) showed phenotype collapse (155 cells vs 635 at 0.3 uM, tub_glcm_contrast z=+25.1, act_glcm_contrast +14.5) with strong cell-count loss. Dose_response e15 cell_count rho=-1.00 p=0 and e13 frac_large_nucleus rho=+0.80 supported dose-dependent large-nucleus accumulation.
- compare_to_reference_atlas e9 was decisive and we weighted it correctly over visual interpretation. NSC vote DNA damage 2/4 included the two active wells with very high similarity 0.969 and 0.94 noted in rationale/conclusions. k-neighbours DNA replication 5/10 vs DNA damage 4/10 explains the retained 0.22 DNA replication hypothesis - lower mean similarity for replication (0.816 vs 0.882 for damage per review) justified ranking damage first but keeping replication as credible polyploidy/S-phase mimic.
- e10-e14 dose_response p-values were non-informative due to n=4 wells (rho=+0.40 p=0.6 for nuc_area, rho=+0.80 p=0.2 for tub_glcm_contrast/frac_large_nucleus, rho=-0.20 p=0.8 for nuc_dna_integrated/frac_mitotic_like). We correctly relied on huge per-well effect sizes rather than p-values, as review notes.

What misled / what we missed:
- describe_phenotype e6 and e7 at mid/high dose flagged Aurora kinase inhibitors as candidates (9 and 10 observations). Visually, DNA-damage G2-arrest nuclear enlargement mimics Aurora inhibition cytokinesis-failure polyploidy/binucleation. We lacked a discriminant visual/quantitative binucleation count - e14 frac_mitotic_like rho=-0.20 actually fell versus expectation for Aurora mitotic arrest, but we did not have phospho-H3 or true binucleate rate in acquisition to resolve it at the time; we had to infer against Aurora from the absence of Aurora neighbours in top-10 and the fall in mitotic proxy.
- e5 and e11 tub_glcm_contrast rho=+0.80 and e8 visual 'Microtubule stabilizers' created a high-dose off-target distractor. Tubulin bundling signal was confined to 10 uM where nuclear phenotype collapsed and density lower, so we discounted it as toxic bundling not primary MoA - correct per review, but acquisition of only one replicate at 10 uM meant we could not statistically test toxicity vs specific effect; concordance of two active lower doses mitigated this.
- search_literature e21 for 'DNA damage G2 arrest nuclear enlargement cell size MCF-7 phenotype' returned 0 hits, so we had no contemporaneous literature bridge linking the measured nuc_area increase to DNA damage; we relied on atlas similarity rather than literature phenotype annotation. The post-hoc literature e20/e22 did return mitomycin C crosslink hits supporting the call.
- We did not acquire a second replicate at any dose (e1 shows 4/4 wells left but we took singletons). This limits power - correctly flagged as concern but mitigated by cross-dose reproducibility of the large-nuclei + high DNA integrated signal at two independent active doses.

Why final integration was sound: update_hypotheses e16 DNA damage 0.52 > DNA replication 0.22 > Aurora 0.18 matched atlas prior with quantitative phenotype; submit_conclusion e17 p=0.58 rationale that NSC high-similarity DNA-damage neighbours outweigh single-source microscopist Aurora call is validated by unblinding. Proposed next experiment (gamma-H2AX + DNA content flow + phospho-H3 vs reference DNA-damage control) remains the right orthogonal test to separate DNA-damage G2 vs Aurora polyploidy and to confirm on-target vs 10 uM tubulin toxicity.

e15 cell_count rho=-1.0 and e5 low count 155 vs 635 correctly identified dose-dependent toxicity and allowed discounting of 10 uM tub_glcm_contrast +25.1 microtubule distractor
e21 0 hits for nuclear enlargement literature forced reliance on quantitative atlas rather than over-interpreting visual binucleation

e9 k-neighbour DNA replication 5/10 vs DNA damage 4/10 created close runner-up - overlapping S-phase vs G2 DNA-content phenotype not resolved phenotypically

## Reflection

Unblinded compound is mitomycin C (CID 5746) - ChEMBL 'DNA inhibitor' on NUCLEIC-ACID, and literature returned in this run confirms mechanism as crosslinker/DNA-damager: PMID 41199376 mitomycin C-induced DSBs and PMID 17512921 mitomycin C-DNA interstrand crosslink, plus general cross-linker biology PMID 8562965. Verdict correct: we called DNA damage at p=0.58, truth DNA damage. Calibration was appropriate - we did not claim high confidence, and runner-up DNA replication at 0.22 was explicitly retained.

What got it right:
- Acquisition choice to sample across dynamic range was discriminative. e2 (0.3 uM) and e3 (3 uM) both showed extreme, concordant nuclear phenotype: nuc_area z=+23.6 and +26.7, nuc_major_axis +12.1/+15.3, nuc_dna_integrated +14.0 at 3 uM - consistent with G2 arrest/DNA content increase, not focal toxicity. e4 (0.003 uM) established inactive baseline (nuc_dna_mean +5.2 only modest) and e5 (10 uM) showed phenotype collapse (155 cells vs 635 at 0.3 uM, tub_glcm_contrast z=+25.1, act_glcm_contrast +14.5) with strong cell-count loss. Dose_response e15 cell_count rho=-1.00 p=0 and e13 frac_large_nucleus rho=+0.80 supported dose-dependent large-nucleus accumulation.
- compare_to_reference_atlas e9 was decisive and we weighted it correctly over visual interpretation. NSC vote DNA damage 2/4 included the two active wells with very high similarity 0.969 and 0.94 noted in rationale/conclusions. k-neighbours DNA replication 5/10 vs DNA damage 4/10 explains the retained 0.22 DNA replication hypothesis - lower mean similarity for replication (0.816 vs 0.882 for damage per review) justified ranking damage first but keeping replication as credible polyploidy/S-phase mimic.
- e10-e14 dose_response p-values were non-informative due to n=4 wells (rho=+0.40 p=0.6 for nuc_area, rho=+0.80 p=0.2 for tub_glcm_contrast/frac_large_nucleus, rho=-0.20 p=0.8 for nuc_dna_integrated/frac_mitotic_like). We correctly relied on huge per-well effect sizes rather than p-values, as review notes.

What misled / what we missed:
- describe_phenotype e6 and e7 at mid/high dose flagged Aurora kinase inhibitors as candidates (9 and 10 observations). Visually, DNA-damage G2-arrest nuclear enlargement mimics Aurora inhibition cytokinesis-failure polyploidy/binucleation. We lacked a discriminant visual/quantitative binucleation count - e14 frac_mitotic_like rho=-0.20 actually fell versus expectation for Aurora mitotic arrest, but we did not have phospho-H3 or true binucleate rate in acquisition to resolve it at the time; we had to infer against Aurora from the absence of Aurora neighbours in top-10 and the fall in mitotic proxy.
- e5 and e11 tub_glcm_contrast rho=+0.80 and e8 visual 'Microtubule stabilizers' created a high-dose off-target distractor. Tubulin bundling signal was confined to 10 uM where nuclear phenotype collapsed and density lower, so we discounted it as toxic bundling not primary MoA - correct per review, but acquisition of only one replicate at 10 uM meant we could not statistically test toxicity vs specific effect; concordance of two active lower doses mitigated this.
- search_literature e21 for 'DNA damage G2 arrest nuclear enlargement cell size MCF-7 phenotype' returned 0 hits, so we had no contemporaneous literature bridge linking the measured nuc_area increase to DNA damage; we relied on atlas similarity rather than literature phenotype annotation. The post-hoc literature e20/e22 did return mitomycin C crosslink hits supporting the call.
- We did not acquire a second replicate at any dose (e1 shows 4/4 wells left but we took singletons). This limits power - correctly flagged as concern but mitigated by cross-dose reproducibility of the large-nuclei + high DNA integrated signal at two independent active doses.

Why final integration was sound: update_hypotheses e16 DNA damage 0.52 > DNA replication 0.22 > Aurora 0.18 matched atlas prior with quantitative phenotype; submit_conclusion e17 p=0.58 rationale that NSC high-similarity DNA-damage neighbours outweigh single-source microscopist Aurora call is validated by unblinding. Proposed next experiment (gamma-H2AX + DNA content flow + phospho-H3 vs reference DNA-damage control) remains the right orthogonal test to separate DNA-damage G2 vs Aurora polyploidy and to confirm on-target vs 10 uM tubulin toxicity.

What was right:
- e2 e3 extreme nuc_area/major_axis and nuc_dna_integrated at 0.3 and 3 uM predicted G2/polyploid DNA damage, concordant across two active doses
- e9 atlas NSC 2/4 DNA damage with similarities 0.969/0.94 correctly outweighed visual Aurora call; no Aurora neighbour in top 10
- e15 cell_count rho=-1.0 and e5 low count 155 vs 635 correctly identified dose-dependent toxicity and allowed discounting of 10 uM tub_glcm_contrast +25.1 microtubule distractor
- e21 0 hits for nuclear enlargement literature forced reliance on quantitative atlas rather than over-interpreting visual binucleation

What was wrong or missed:
- e6 e7 Aurora candidates misled visual interpretation - large nuclei from G2 arrest mimic cytokinesis-failure polyploidy without phospho-H3/binucleate quantification
- e9 k-neighbour DNA replication 5/10 vs DNA damage 4/10 created close runner-up - overlapping S-phase vs G2 DNA-content phenotype not resolved phenotypically
- e10 e11 e13 dose_response p=0.2-0.6 non-significant due to n=4 acquisition choice; required effect-size reasoning not statistical significance

Proposed next experiment: gamma-H2AX + cell-cycle DNA content flow at 0.3 and 3 uM vs reference DNA-damage compound and DMSO, plus phospho-H3 to exclude Aurora, as originally proposed
